name: Sega Dreamcast
description: Sega's last home console, launched in Japan in 1998 and in the West in 1999. It shipped with a built-in modem for online play and debuted influential games such as Shenmue and Jet Set Radio. Sega stopped making it in 2001 and left the hardware business.

specs.memory: 16 MB RAM / 8 MB VRAM / 2 MB sound RAM

curiosities: The North American launch date was 9/9/99.
Its VMU memory card has its own small screen and can run minigames on its own.
Games could use Microsoft's Windows CE as an alternative to Sega's own libraries.
GD-ROM discs hold about 1 GB, more than a standard CD.
It was the first console sold with a built-in modem for online play.
story: After the Saturn's failure in the West, Sega built a console that would be easy to program: a Hitachi SH-4, NEC's PowerVR graphics and a modem in every box. It launched in Japan in November 1998 and in North America on 9.9.99.

The American launch was a record, and online play, the VMU and games such as Soulcalibur, Shenmue, Jet Set Radio, Crazy Taxi and Phantasy Star Online showed what it could do. But Sony's PlayStation 2 was coming, and disc piracy hurt sales.
Sega stopped making it in March 2001 and left console hardware. Homebrew and independent releases on its discs have never stopped.
